chapters.title: The Essentialist
chapters.sourcePressure: The chapter introduces the Essentialist versus Nonessentialist contrast, the paradox that success creates options that erode clarity, and the three truths: choice, few things matter, and doing anything is not doing everything.
chapters.coreMove: Make the hidden cost of capable overcommitment visible, then replace scattered availability with a filter for highest contribution.
chapters.commonMisread: A weak run would write a generic introduction about being productive, simplifying life, or trying harder to prioritize.

chapters.title: Choose: The Invincible Power of Choice
chapters.sourcePressure: The chapter restores agency by treating choice as an action, warning that forgotten agency can become learned helplessness, and teaching the reader to choose to choose under constraint.
chapters.coreMove: Convert a pressured obligation into an owned choice so the next yes or no is deliberate instead of automatic.
chapters.commonMisread: A weak run would pretend all constraints disappear if the reader has a better attitude.

chapters.title: Discern: The Unimportance of Practically Everything
chapters.sourcePressure: The chapter applies the law of the vital few to show that almost everything is noise and only a small number of options deserve concentrated effort.
chapters.coreMove: Rank options sharply enough to release good-looking noise before it dilutes the contribution that matters.
chapters.commonMisread: A weak run would say everything is important in different ways and ask the reader to balance it all.

chapters.title: Trade-Off: Which Problem Do I Want?
chapters.sourcePressure: The chapter insists that trade-offs are real and that the essentialist stops asking how to do both and starts choosing which problem is worth carrying.
chapters.coreMove: Name the cost inside each option and choose the burden attached to the more essential contribution.
chapters.commonMisread: A weak run would frame trade-offs as temporary obstacles that clever scheduling can overcome.

chapters.title: Escape: The Perks of Being Unavailable
chapters.sourcePressure: The chapter opens exploration by defending solitude, reading, and reflective distance as conditions for seeing what matters.
chapters.coreMove: Create protected unavailability so judgment can hear something other than the loudest incoming request.
chapters.commonMisread: A weak run would write about taking breaks, resting more, or ignoring messages as a lifestyle hack.

chapters.title: Look: See What Really Matters
chapters.sourcePressure: The chapter turns protected space into disciplined scanning: filter for the fascinating, journal selectively, and find patterns instead of drowning in facts and opinions.
chapters.coreMove: Stop recording every input and look for the quiet pattern that explains what is really happening.
chapters.commonMisread: A weak run would tell the reader to pay more attention to details without teaching signal selection.

chapters.title: Play: Embrace the Wisdom of Your Inner Child
chapters.sourcePressure: The chapter defends play as essential fuel for broader options, lower stress, executive function, and creative exploration.
chapters.coreMove: Use playful exploration to loosen a narrowed mind so better options can appear.
chapters.commonMisread: A weak run would reduce play to leisure, reward, or childish fun after the real work is done.

chapters.title: Sleep: Protect the Asset
chapters.sourcePressure: The chapter argues that sleep protects the human asset required for discernment, creativity, connection, and contribution.
chapters.coreMove: Treat sleep as strategic protection for judgment instead of the leftover hour after ambition is done spending the body.
chapters.commonMisread: A weak run would give generic sleep hygiene tips or moralize about getting eight hours.

chapters.title: Select: The Power of Extreme Criteria
chapters.sourcePressure: The chapter closes exploration by turning discernment into harsh selection through minimum criteria, extreme criteria, and the 90 percent rule.
chapters.coreMove: Replace soft approval with a high bar that rejects near-matches before they become commitments.
chapters.commonMisread: A weak run would tell the reader to choose good opportunities more carefully without defining an extreme test.

chapters.title: Clarify: One Decision That Makes a Thousand
chapters.sourcePressure: The chapter begins elimination by showing that vague purpose produces politics, scattered effort, and short-term wins that do not add up.
chapters.coreMove: Write an essential intent concrete enough to settle hundreds of later decisions before they become debates.
chapters.commonMisread: A weak run would write about vision statements or inspirational goals without behavioral specificity.

chapters.title: Dare: The Power of a Graceful "No"
chapters.sourcePressure: The chapter makes essentialism real through courageous, clear, relationally graceful refusal that separates the decision from the relationship.
chapters.coreMove: Say no in a way that protects the essential work and preserves respect instead of buying temporary approval with a weak yes.
chapters.commonMisread: A weak run would make this a blunt assertiveness chapter or a list of polite scripts with no trade-off logic.

chapters.title: Uncommit: Win Big by Cutting Your Losses
chapters.sourcePressure: The chapter confronts sunk-cost bias, status quo bias, zero-based thinking, reverse pilots, and slower commitments so yesterday's investments stop governing tomorrow.
chapters.coreMove: Ask whether you would choose the commitment again from scratch, then withdraw cleanly when the honest answer is no.
chapters.commonMisread: A weak run would say quit things that are hard or boring without distinguishing sunk cost from worthwhile persistence.

chapters.title: Edit: The Invisible Art
chapters.sourcePressure: The chapter reframes editing as a creative act of cutting, condensing, and correcting so the important becomes clearer and stronger.
chapters.coreMove: Remove, condense, and correct until the essential point has room to be seen and used.
chapters.commonMisread: A weak run would treat editing as tidying, decluttering, or simply deleting random commitments.

chapters.title: Limit: The Freedom of Setting Boundaries
chapters.sourcePressure: The chapter shows that boundaries protect time from being hijacked and reduce the need to renegotiate every request from scratch.
chapters.coreMove: Set visible limits early enough that other people can plan around them and the essential is no longer endlessly available.
chapters.commonMisread: A weak run would write about personal boundaries as generic self-care without connecting them to protected contribution.

chapters.title: Buffer: The Unfair Advantage
chapters.sourcePressure: The chapter begins execution by treating the unexpected as predictable enough to plan for through buffers, scenario planning, larger estimates, and resilience.
chapters.coreMove: Build margin before reality interrupts, so surprise does not turn essential work into emergency response.
chapters.commonMisread: A weak run would say leave extra time as a scheduling tip without teaching the planning fallacy or contingency logic.

chapters.title: Subtract: Bring Forth More by Removing Obstacles
chapters.sourcePressure: The chapter teaches constraint removal through the slowest hiker idea: identify the bottleneck that controls throughput instead of adding effort everywhere.
chapters.coreMove: Find the obstacle that slows the whole system and remove it before asking people to push harder.
chapters.commonMisread: A weak run would write about simplifying tasks or removing distractions rather than locating the controlling constraint.

chapters.title: Progress: The Power of Small Wins
chapters.sourcePressure: The chapter uses progress research, minimum viable progress, and minimum viable preparation to show why small visible wins sustain motivation.
chapters.coreMove: Shrink the next step until it creates visible movement on meaningful work, then let momentum compound.
chapters.commonMisread: A weak run would make small wins sound like lowering ambition or celebrating trivial activity.

chapters.title: Flow: The Genius of Routine
chapters.sourcePressure: The chapter presents routine as the structure that makes essential work the default and reduces repeated decision fatigue.
chapters.coreMove: Design a default path that carries the essential action before distractions get a daily vote.
chapters.commonMisread: A weak run would write about morning routines or habit stacking without connecting routine to protected essential work.

chapters.title: Focus: What's Important Now?
chapters.sourcePressure: The chapter narrows execution to the present moment by distinguishing multitasking from the fantasy of multifocusing and asking what is important now.
chapters.coreMove: Pause inside pressure, name the one important now, and give that next move undivided attention.
chapters.commonMisread: A weak run would write broad focus advice about avoiding distractions or single-tasking all day.

chapters.title: Be: The Essentialist Life
chapters.sourcePressure: The closing chapter lifts essentialism from occasional technique into identity, meaning, clarity, control, joy, and a life with fewer regrets.
chapters.coreMove: Move from doing essentialist tactics to becoming the kind of person who repeatedly asks what is essential and eliminates the rest.
chapters.commonMisread: A weak run would close with generic inspiration about living your best life or maintaining productivity habits.
